hypothesis: A simple supervised classifier built on open acoustic embeddings can achieve a reproducible, non-trivial separation between synthetic and natural voices (e.g., EER significantly better than random guessing) on a held-out test set drawn from diverse open-source datasets, and can be packaged as a low-latency service suitable for proof-of-concept integration into enterprise contact center architectures.

baseline.description: A minimal but enterprise-relevant synthetic-vs-human voice detection pipeline using off-the-shelf audio embeddings and a simple classifier, implemented with open datasets and models. This serves as the reference configuration against which future enhancements (ensembles, domain adaptation, proprietary models) are compared.

datasets.name: ASVspoof 2019 LA
datasets.role: Primary source of labeled bona fide (human) and spoofed (synthetic/converted) speech for training and evaluation.

splits.train: Use only the official train split for model training.
splits.dev: Use the official dev split for validation, hyperparameter tuning, and early stopping.
splits.eval: Use the official eval split as the held-out test set for reporting primary metrics.

datasets.notes: Focus on logical access (LA) subset; treat all spoofed attack types as synthetic voice. Do not use ASV scores—only the raw waveforms and spoof labels.

datasets.name: VCTK + publicly available synthetic variants (e.g., VCTK-based TTS samples from academic releases)
datasets.role: Secondary dataset to test limited cross-dataset generalization and robustness to different speakers and recording conditions.

splits.train: Optional small augmentation (<= 20% of total training examples) if desired; ensure no speaker overlap with evaluation splits.
splits.eval: Use a held-out subset purely for out-of-domain evaluation; do not mix with ASVspoof for headline metrics.

datasets.notes: If used, document exact source URLs and license terms in the repo.

data_preparation.audio_format: Convert all audio to mono, 16 kHz PCM WAV, 16-bit.
data_preparation.duration_handling: For each file, extract a single centered segment of fixed length (e.g., 3.0 seconds). If shorter, pad with low-level noise or zero-padding; if longer, center-crop.
data_preparation.train_dev_eval_isolation: No file, speaker, or attack scenario may appear in more than one of the train/dev/eval sets. Respect the dataset’s own partitioning.
data_preparation.class_balance: Within each split, ensure class balance within ±10%; if necessary, downsample the majority class.

feature_extraction.frontend: Pretrained x-vector or ECAPA-TDNN style speaker embedding network from an open-source speech toolkit (e.g., SpeechBrain or pyannote.audio).
feature_extraction.input_representation: Log-mel spectrogram, 80 mel bins, 25 ms window, 10 ms hop; normalization per-utterance.
feature_extraction.embedding_dim: Typically 192–512 depending on chosen model (record exact dimension in evidence).
feature_extraction.processing: One fixed-size embedding per utterance (mean-pool over frame-level embeddings if applicable).

model.type: Shallow classifier operating on frozen embeddings.
options: Logistic regression with L2 regularization (primary choice).

training_regime.optimizer: LBFGS or equivalent for logistic regression; default solver in scikit-learn is acceptable if deterministic.
training_regime.selection: Grid search over C using dev split; select model with lowest EER on dev. Tie-breaker is highest AUC-ROC.

serving.packaging: Stateless HTTP service exposing a /score endpoint that accepts audio and returns a synthetic probability score.
serving.implementation: Reference implementation in Python (e.g., FastAPI), with embeddings and classifier loaded into memory on startup.
serving.latency_target: End-to-end per-utterance scoring p95 latency < 300 ms on a single CPU-only server for 3-second clips.

treatment.description: The same detection pipeline as the baseline, with one controlled improvement: fine-tuning the embedding model on the synthetic-vs-human task using the train split before training the classifier. This treatment is defined only to ensure experimental comparability but is not required to be superior.

differences_from_baseline.data: Identical datasets, preprocessing, and splits as the baseline.
differences_from_baseline.feature_extraction: Initialize from the same pretrained embedding network but unfreeze the last N layers (e.g., last 1–2 blocks) and fine-tune on the classification objective using the train split.

model.type: End-to-end model with a small classification head added on top of the embedding network.

training_regime.schedule: Fixed or simple step decay; early stopping based on dev EER.

differences_from_baseline.serving: Expose the same API contract as the baseline. Measure differences in latency and resource utilization under the same workloads.

workloads.name: wl-inference-asvspoof-eval
workloads.description: Batch scoring of the official ASVspoof 2019 LA eval split to generate metrics and curves.

inputs.num_samples: All available samples in the eval split.
inputs.sampling_strategy: Use every file once; no augmentation.
inputs.input_format: File paths to WAV audio preprocessed as per baseline.

per_sample: predicted_label (for fixed threshold(s) recorded in evidence).

workloads.name: wl-inference-asvspoof-dev
workloads.description: Batch scoring of the ASVspoof 2019 LA dev split for hyperparameter tuning and threshold calibration.

inputs.num_samples: All available samples in the dev split.
inputs.sampling_strategy: Use every file once; no augmentation.

workloads.name: wl-inference-ood-vctk
workloads.description: Optional out-of-domain evaluation using VCTK-based synthetic and natural voices to test robustness.

workloads.name: wl-online-throughput-smoke
workloads.description: Synthetic load test against the deployed HTTP API to confirm practical service viability for enterprise integration pilots.

inputs.source_dataset: Random 1,000 clips per class from ASVspoof2019_LA_eval.
inputs.request_pattern: Poisson arrivals approximated via a fixed QPS ramp.

execution.concurrency: As required to achieve target_qps (e.g., 10–50 parallel clients).
execution.metrics_collection: Collect latency, error rate, and CPU/memory utilization.

data_controls: Use the exact same train/dev/eval splits for baseline and treatment.
Ensure class balance per split within ±10%.
Do not leak eval or dev data into training or fine-tuning.
Document dataset versions, download URLs, and integrity hashes.
randomness_controls: Set and log fixed random seeds (Python, NumPy, and ML framework).
Disable non-deterministic CuDNN algorithms where applicable or record their use.
Shuffle training data with the same seed for all runs.
preprocessing_controls: Use identical audio preprocessing across baseline and treatment (resampling, mono conversion, normalization, fixed-length cropping/padding).
Use identical feature front-end parameters (mel bins, window size, hop length).
training_controls: Use the same number of training epochs or early-stopping patience across comparable models.
Use the same batch size within hardware limits.
Record all hyperparameters and keep them constant except where explicitly part of the treatment.
evaluation_controls: Compute metrics on the same evaluation sets and in the same order.
Do not tune thresholds on eval; thresholds must be derived from dev or pre-defined policies.
Log the entire score distribution for post-hoc analysis.
operational_controls: Run latency and throughput measurements on the same hardware profile.
Ensure no unrelated background jobs run on the evaluation machine during performance tests.
Use the same API envelope and serialization formats across baseline and treatment.

metrics.name: eer
metrics.description: Equal Error Rate: point where false acceptance rate equals false rejection rate.
metrics.aggregation: Computed from all scores on a given eval split.

metrics.name: auc_roc
metrics.description: Area under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve.
metrics.aggregation: Computed from all scores on a given eval split.

metrics.name: tpr_at_fixed_fpr_001
metrics.description: True Positive Rate when False Positive Rate is constrained at 1%.
metrics.aggregation: Computed from ROC curve on a given eval split.

metrics.name: tpr_at_fixed_fpr_0001
metrics.description: True Positive Rate when False Positive Rate is constrained at 0.1%.
metrics.aggregation: Computed from ROC curve on a given eval split.

metrics.name: accuracy_at_policized_threshold
metrics.description: Overall classification accuracy at a threshold selected from the dev set to approximate an enterprise-relevant operating point (e.g., FPR <= 1%).
metrics.aggregation: Computed separately on dev and eval splits.

metrics.name: fpr_at_policized_threshold
metrics.description: False Positive Rate at the dev-selected threshold.
metrics.aggregation: Computed separately on dev and eval splits.

metrics.name: fnr_at_policized_threshold
metrics.description: False Negative Rate at the dev-selected threshold.
metrics.aggregation: Computed separately on dev and eval splits.

metrics.name: p50_latency_ms
metrics.description: Median per-request end-to-end scoring latency for the online API under workload wl-online-throughput-smoke.

metrics.name: throughput_qps
metrics.description: Average queries per second sustained during the sustained phase of the load test.
metrics.aggregation: Average over the sustained phase window.

metrics.name: cpu_utilization_pct
metrics.description: Average CPU utilization of the scoring service process during the sustained load phase.

metrics.name: memory_utilization_mb
metrics.description: Average resident memory used by the scoring service during the sustained load phase.

statistical: On ASVspoof2019_LA_eval, the baseline pipeline achieves eer <= 0.20 (20%) and auc_roc >= 0.85. These thresholds are illustrative for a non-trivial baseline; if not met, document reasons and dataset/model mismatches.
The difference in eer between repeated baseline runs with identical seeds and environment should be <= 0.01 absolute, demonstrating practical reproducibility.
If the treatment is evaluated, any claimed improvement must be supported by consistent betterment of eer and auc_roc on both dev and eval splits, not just one.
operational: Under wl-online-throughput-smoke on reference hardware, p95_latency_ms <= 300 ms and http_5xx_rate <= 0.5%.
The service must correctly log every detection request and response according to the evidence_schema, with no missing or malformed entries in more than 0.1% of requests.
API contract remains stable; no schema-breaking changes occur between baseline and treatment runs.
governance_and_enterprise_relevance: All datasets and models used must have licenses compatible with internal enterprise experimentation (no undisclosed proprietary data).
Data retention options and log content must be configurable to comply with typical enterprise privacy requirements (e.g., ability to drop raw audio and retain only derived features and scores).
The experiment setup, hyperparameters, and exact commit hashes of the repository must be captured so that another team can reproduce results within reasonable variance.

failure_modes.name: data_leakage_between_splits
failure_modes.description: Accidental reuse of the same utterances or speakers across train, dev, and eval, leading to overly optimistic metrics.
failure_modes.detection: Cross-check file IDs and speaker IDs for overlap; report overlap rate in evidence.
failure_modes.mitigation: Re-build splits and re-train; discard contaminated results.

failure_modes.name: overfitting_to_asvspoof_attacks
failure_modes.description: Model exploits narrow artifacts specific to ASVspoof attack implementations, resulting in poor generalization to different synthetic voices (e.g., VCTK-based or future TTS models).
failure_modes.detection: Large gap between ASVspoof eval performance and ood VCTK performance (e.g., eer_ood > eer_asvspoof + 0.15).
failure_modes.mitigation: Document this limitation explicitly; consider diversifying training data in later chapters, but keep the baseline as-is for comparability.

failure_modes.name: domain_mismatch_to_enterprise_audio
failure_modes.description: Baseline results on curated datasets do not translate to noisy, codec-compressed, or multilingual contact center audio.
failure_modes.detection: Qualitative review and, if possible, pilot testing on a small internal dataset reveal degraded performance.
failure_modes.mitigation: Flag the baseline as a best-case indicator only; use it as a relative benchmark for alternative methods rather than an absolute readiness signal.

failure_modes.name: non_deterministic_hardware_behavior
failure_modes.description: Differences in GPU/CPU libraries and kernel versions introduce subtle non-determinism in training and inference.
failure_modes.detection: Repeated runs with identical seeds produce metric differences above expected variance (e.g., eer difference > 0.02).
failure_modes.mitigation: Pin framework versions, document hardware and drivers, and where necessary switch to CPU-only inference for published baseline numbers.

failure_modes.name: latency_regressions_in_serving
failure_modes.description: Embedding extraction and model scoring are too slow for practical integration into contact center flows.
failure_modes.detection: Online throughput tests fail p95 latency targets or encounter sustained high CPU utilization.
failure_modes.mitigation: Profile the service, enable model quantization or batching, or clearly document that the baseline is offline/batch-only for some environments.

failure_modes.name: logging_and_privacy_misconfiguration
failure_modes.description: Detection logs inadvertently include sensitive personal data (e.g., full call recordings, customer identifiers) without appropriate controls.
failure_modes.detection: Audit of log samples reveals presence of raw audio or PII beyond what is specified in evidence_schema.
failure_modes.mitigation: Strip or hash identifiers; log only necessary metadata and derived features; align with internal privacy policies before production-like use.

minimum.cpu: 4 physical cores (x86_64 or ARM64) with AVX2 or equivalent.
minimum.gpu: Not required for inference; optional for faster fine-tuning (e.g., 1 consumer-grade GPU with >= 8 GB VRAM).

reference_for_metrics.cpu: 8-core server-class CPU (e.g., Intel Xeon or AMD EPYC) for published latency/throughput.
reference_for_metrics.gpu: Single NVIDIA T4 or equivalent if treatment fine-tuning is performed.

software.os: Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+ recommended); macOS acceptable for development but not for reference metrics.

ml_framework: torch (PyTorch) or equivalent, with pinned version and CUDA/cuDNN versions if applicable
speech_toolkit: speechbrain or pyannote.audio (exact model name and version pinned)
observability: prometheus_client or equivalent metrics exporter (optional but recommended)

system_dependencies: ffmpeg or sox for consistent audio conversion.

chapter_5/: notebooks/ (exploratory EDA and plotting of ROC/EER).
scripts/ (data prep, feature extraction, training, evaluation).
configs/ (YAML/JSON configs for experiments and environments).

run_instructions.overview: These steps define a reproducible path to run the baseline experiment, train the model, evaluate metrics, and deploy the reference service. All commands are indicative; exact paths/scripts must match the repository implementation.

steps.title: Clone repository and set up environment
actions: Clone the companion repository: `git clone https://github.com/bookauthority/securing-call.git`.
Checkout the tag or branch corresponding to the book release: e.g., `git checkout v1.0-ch5-baseline`.
Create and activate a Python virtual environment (e.g., `python3.10 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate`).
Install dependencies: `pip install -r chapter_5/requirements.txt`.
Verify versions: run `python chapter_5/scripts/print_env.py` (or equivalent) to record Python, package, and CUDA versions.

steps.title: Download and prepare datasets
actions: Download ASVspoof 2019 LA data following the dataset’s license and usage terms. Store raw archives under `data/raw/asvspoof2019_LA/`.
Optionally download VCTK and any associated synthetic-voice releases, storing under `data/raw/vctk/`.
Run the data preparation script: `python chapter_5/scripts/prepare_data_asvspoof.py --config chapter_5/configs/asvspoof_prep.yaml`.
Confirm that processed WAV files and manifest CSV/JSON files are created under `data/processed/asvspoof2019_LA/` with explicit split labels (train/dev/eval).
Inspect a small sample of manifests to ensure correct labels and no obvious leakage.

steps.title: Extract embeddings
actions: Configure the embedding model in `chapter_5/configs/embeddings.yaml` (e.g., specify SpeechBrain x-vector model name and checkpoint).
Run embedding extraction for train/dev/eval: `python chapter_5/scripts/extract_embeddings.py --config chapter_5/configs/embeddings_asvspoof.yaml`.
This should produce feature files (e.g., `.npy` or HDF5) and corresponding index files under `features/asvspoof2019_LA/{train,dev,eval}/`.
Optionally run a verification script `python chapter_5/scripts/check_embeddings.py` to print embedding shapes, basic statistics, and sample labels.

steps.title: Train baseline classifier
actions: Set baseline classifier parameters in `chapter_5/configs/baseline_logreg.yaml` (including C grid, class_weight, and random seed).
Train the classifier: `python chapter_5/scripts/train_classifier.py --config chapter_5/configs/baseline_logreg.yaml`.

The script should: (a) load train/dev embeddings, (b) run cross-validated hyperparameter search on dev, (c) select the best C based on dev EER, (d) save the trained model and scaler under `models/baseline_logreg/`.
Capture a training summary JSON (e.g., `training_summary.json`) including hyperparameters, dev metrics, and paths to artifacts.

steps.title: Evaluate baseline and compute metrics
actions: Run evaluation on dev and eval splits: `python chapter_5/scripts/evaluate_classifier.py --config chapter_5/configs/baseline_logreg_eval.yaml`.
The evaluation script should output: (a) per-sample scores and labels to `results/baseline_logreg/{dev,eval}_scores.csv`, and (b) aggregate metrics to `results/baseline_logreg/metrics.json`.
Generate ROC and DET curves and save as PNG/SVG in `results/baseline_logreg/plots/`.
Use a utility script or notebook (e.g., `chapter_5/notebooks/05_eer_roc_analysis.ipynb`) to compute EER, AUC-ROC, TPR at fixed FPRs, and thresholds for desired operating points.

steps.title: Deploy baseline as a service
actions: Configure the API service in `chapter_5/service/config.yaml`, pointing to the trained embedding model and classifier artifact paths.
Start the service locally: `uvicorn chapter_5.service.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000`.
Test the `/health` and `/score` endpoints using provided sample audio: `python chapter_5/scripts/test_api.py --audio examples/sample_synthetic.wav`.
Optionally, build a Docker image: `docker build -t securing-call-ch5-baseline:latest chapter_5/service/` and run with pinned resource limits.

steps.title: Run online smoke test
actions: Prepare a subset of eval clips for load testing using `chapter_5/scripts/prepare_load_test_set.py`.
Execute the load test with a tool such as Locust, k6, or a custom script, e.g.: `python chapter_5/scripts/run_load_test.py --config chapter_5/configs/load_test.yaml`.
Collect latency and resource metrics and export them to `results/baseline_logreg/online_metrics.json`.
Verify that online metrics meet or are close to the target operational thresholds defined in success_criteria; if not, document deviations.

evidence_schema.description: Schema for capturing and storing experimental evidence so that teams can audit runs, reproduce results, and reason about applicability to their own environments.

fields.run_id: Unique identifier for the experiment run (UUID).
fields.timestamp_utc: ISO 8601 timestamp when the run was initiated.
fields.git_commit: Git commit hash of the repository at run time.

hardware.gpu_model: String identifier if present, else null.

software.package_versions: Map of package names to exact versions.

configs.data_prep_config_path: Path to data prep config file used.
configs.model_config_path: Path to classifier or end-to-end model config.

datasets.name: e.g., ASVspoof2019_LA
datasets.speaker_count: Number of unique speakers, if available.

hashes.manifest_md5: MD5 or SHA256 of manifest file.

fields_per_line.eer: Computed EER on split at this epoch, if computed.
fields_per_line.auc_roc: AUC-ROC on split at this epoch, if computed.

fields.intended_use: Short text describing intended experimental use (not production).
fields.training_data_summary: Reference to data_manifest entries used for training.
fields.known_limitations: List referencing failure_modes relevant to this model.
fields.metrics_summary: Key metrics on dev and eval splits (EER, AUC-ROC, etc.).

thresholds.name: policy_threshold_1
thresholds.description: Threshold tuned from dev set for FPR ~1%.
thresholds.dev_fpr: False positive rate on dev at this threshold.
thresholds.dev_fnr: False negative rate on dev at this threshold.

fields.file_id: Unique identifier of the audio file within the dataset.
fields.model_score: Continuous score from the classifier (probability or logit).
fields.timestamp_utc: Time of scoring (optional for offline runs).

dev.tpr_at_fixed_fpr_001: Numeric TPR at FPR 1% on dev.
dev.tpr_at_fixed_fpr_0001: Numeric TPR at FPR 0.1% on dev.
dev.accuracy_at_policized_threshold: Accuracy on dev at threshold derived from dev.
dev.fpr_at_policized_threshold: FPR on dev at that threshold.
dev.fnr_at_policized_threshold: FNR on dev at that threshold.

eval.tpr_at_fixed_fpr_001: Numeric TPR at FPR 1% on eval.
eval.tpr_at_fixed_fpr_0001: Numeric TPR at FPR 0.1% on eval.
eval.accuracy_at_policized_threshold: Accuracy on eval at threshold selected from dev.
eval.fpr_at_policized_threshold: FPR on eval at that threshold.
eval.fnr_at_policized_threshold: FNR on eval at that threshold.

fields_per_line.request_id: Unique identifier for the API request.
fields_per_line.timestamp_utc: Time at which request was processed.

caller_context.channel: e.g., lab_test; in enterprise integration, may include 'ivr', 'agent_desktop', etc.
caller_context.session_id: Optional correlation ID; hashed or pseudonymized in examples.

audio_metadata.duration_seconds: Duration of the audio segment processed.

detection_result.confidence_band: Optional coarse bucket (e.g., low|medium|high) based on score.

fields.http_5xx_rate: Fraction of requests resulting in 5xx responses.
